agent.result_text:
The remainder change is in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` now pass. Getting there took a second fix, to how claims are renumbered, that you should know about.

**The remainder rule** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/pool/PoolService.java`): what's left over after rounding the cuts now goes to the member with the smallest non-zero cut. On a tie, the member added latest gets it. Members with no cut (retired, held, or whose dates don't cover today) never get it. If no cut in the pool is non-zero, it goes to the last member who has a share. I updated the javadoc to match. Only the server calculates cuts, so nothing changed in the front end, and there were no data or schema changes.

**The renumbering fix** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimService.java`, `reassign`): on the first run, scenario 2 failed on something unrelated to pools. When a bulk reassign moves a claim to the person it already belongs to, the test expects it to take the next number (X-1 becomes X-2, and the audit line carries `number=X-2`). The code skipped renumbering in that case. That didn't match the test or the method's own javadoc, which says a moved claim "takes the next number". I removed the same-person check, so a numbered claim is always renumbered when reassigned. Normal single reassigns to the same person are still refused, so in practice this only affects bulk moves.
